xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4831: Phone app: native sign-in redirect and ios/android platforms in the account service

plan.title: Phone app: native sign-in redirect and ios/android platforms in the account service
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

narratives.Problem: The overdeck.ai account service (services/account) accepts only loopback redirect_uri values in its PKCE sign-in flow and only desktop platforms (linux|darwin|win32 x x64|arm64). The Overdeck phone app (epic PAN-4823) signs in through the system browser and must be redirected back to its private-use URI scheme ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback, and must register itself as an ios-arm64 or android-arm64 device.
narratives.Proposal: In services/account/src/pkce.ts add NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT = 'ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback' and validateClientRedirect (exact raw-string match, else the existing loopback rule), used in parseStart and readPayload only; the token exchange already compares against the stored, validated redirect and stays unchanged. In services/account/src/devices.ts widen PLATFORM_RE to ^((linux|darwin|win32)-(x64|arm64)|(ios|android)-arm64)$ and make defaultLabel return 'iPhone' and 'Android phone'. Unit tests cover the accept/reject set and a full PKCE exchange with the native redirect (epic AC-4). docs/ACCOUNT-SERVICE.md describes the new redirect and platforms.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No CORS or any other new response header on the account service; the phone app must call /oauth/token and /v1/* with native HTTP (CapacitorHttp)
- No change to src/lib/account/client.ts (machine-side PLATFORM_ARCH_RE stays desktop-only)
- No change to the device flow (device-flow.ts) or its /activate wording, even though it now accepts the phone platforms through the shared validator
- No change to exchangeAuthorizationCode or redirectToClient in pkce.ts
- No prefix, scheme-only or parsed-URL matching of the native redirect; exact string only
- No D1 migration
- No universal links / App Links / https redirect for the app
- No phone app code, no user-facing Mintlify pages, no services/connect change (other epic items)
- No deploy of the account Worker (operator-only)

autoDecisions.summary: PAN-4774 sequencing gate treated as satisfied
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says not to start before the Anywhere release acceptance run (PAN-4774) passes; gh reports PAN-4774 CLOSED on 2026-11-02.

autoDecisions.summary: Only parseStart and readPayload switch to validateClientRedirect; the code exchange is unchanged
autoDecisions.rationale: W-ACC1 says to also use it in the code exchange, but exchangeAuthorizationCode (pkce.ts line 128) never called validateLoopbackRedirect; it compares the posted redirect_uri to the stored, already-validated value, which is the RFC 6749 4.1.3 rule.

autoDecisions.summary: The device flow accepts ios-arm64/android-arm64 through the shared isValidPlatform, with no extra gate
autoDecisions.rationale: The phone app never uses the device flow and no caller sends phone platforms there; a second validator would be code for no caller.
Epic AC-4 does not need it, http.ts documents 'no Access-Control-* header' as an invariant, and CORS changes the auth surface; W-APP1 uses native HTTP instead. Note posted on the epic.
It validates the machine's own process.platform/arch; widening it would let a Node process on Android (Termux) register as an 'Android phone'.

items.title: Accept exactly ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback as a PKCE redirect_uri

expected_outputs: tests/unit/services/account/pkce.test.ts passes, including the new native-redirect accept/reject test

narrative.Action: PRD work item W-1. In services/account/src/pkce.ts: (1) update the module header on line 2 to name both the loopback redirect (RFC 8252 7.3) and the phone app's private-use scheme redirect (PRD PAN-4823 D-6; RFC 8252 7.1). (2) Directly after validateLoopbackRedirect (ends line 36) add `export const NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT = 'ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback';` with the doc comment `/** The phone app's private-use scheme redirect (RFC 8252 §7.1), allowed exactly. */` and `export function validateClientRedirect(raw: string | null): string | null { if (raw === NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT) return raw; return validateLoopbackRedirect(raw); }`. (3) Replace validateLoopbackRedirect( with validateClientRedirect( in parseStart (line 47) and readPayload (line 73) only. Do NOT change exchangeAuthorizationCode or redirectToClient. In tests/unit/services/account/pkce.test.ts import NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT and validateClientRedirect and add the test 'accepts exactly the native redirect ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback and refuses near misses with 400' asserting: startQuery({ redirect_uri: NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT }) -> 302; each of 'ai.overdeck.app:/other', 'ai.overdeck.app://oauth/callback', 'evil:/oauth/callback', 'AI.OVERDECK.APP:/oauth/callback', 'ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback?x=1', 'ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback#' -> 400, Location null, body contains 'redirect_uri'; validateClientRedirect(NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT) === NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT, validateClientRedirect('http://127.0.0.1:4567/callback') returns that string, validateClientRedirect(null) === null.

items.title: Given redirect_uri=ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback, when GET /auth/start is called with otherwise valid params, then it returns 302 to GitHub

Given redirect_uri is any of ai.overdeck.app:/other, ai.overdeck.app://oauth/callback, evil:/oauth/callback, AI.OVERDECK.APP:/oauth/callback, ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback?x=1 or ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback#, when GET /auth/start is called, then it returns 400 with no Location header and a body naming redirect_uri
validateClientRedirect returns NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT for the exact string, returns a loopback URL unchanged, and returns null for null
The diff of exchangeAuthorizationCode and redirectToClient is empty, and every pre-existing test in pkce.test.ts passes with unchanged expectations
Accept ios-arm64 and android-arm64 platforms with iPhone and Android phone default labels

narrative.Action: PRD work item W-2. In services/account/src/devices.ts change line 18 from `export const PLATFORM_RE = /^(linux|darwin|win32)-(x64|arm64)$/;` to `export const PLATFORM_RE = /^((linux|darwin|win32)-(x64|arm64)|(ios|android)-arm64)$/;`. In defaultLabel (lines 57-62) add `if (platform.startsWith('ios-')) return 'iPhone';` and `if (platform.startsWith('android-')) return 'Android phone';` after the win32 branch and before `return 'Linux device';`. In tests/unit/services/account/devices.test.ts assert isValidPlatform true for 'ios-arm64' and 'android-arm64', false for 'ios-x64', 'android-x64', 'ios-arm', 'iphone-arm64'; and in the 'default labels follow D-17' test assert defaultLabel('ios-arm64') === 'iPhone' and defaultLabel('android-arm64') === 'Android phone'. Do not touch src/lib/account/client.ts or device-flow.ts.

items.title: isValidPlatform returns true for ios-arm64 and android-arm64 and false for ios-x64, android-x64, ios-arm and iphone-arm64, asserted in devices.test.ts
defaultLabel returns 'iPhone' for ios-arm64 and 'Android phone' for android-arm64, and still returns 'Linux device', 'macOS device', 'Windows device' for the desktop platforms
src/lib/account/client.ts and services/account/src/device-flow.ts are unchanged in the diff, and device-flow.test.ts passes
End-to-end PKCE test: native redirect with ios-arm64 mints an iPhone device

expected_outputs: every test file under tests/unit/services/account/ passes, including the two new native sign-in tests

narrative.Action: PRD work item W-3 (epic AC-4). In tests/unit/services/account/pkce.test.ts add test 'native sign-in: ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback with ios-arm64 mints a device labelled iPhone': setup(); back = await signIn(env, deps, { redirect_uri: NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT, platform: 'ios-arm64' }); assert back.protocol + back.pathname === 'ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback' (NOT back.origin, which is the string 'null' for a private-use scheme); state is 'client-state-123', code matches /^odc_[0-9a-f]{64}$/, error is null; exchange(env, deps, { code, redirect_uri: NATIVE_APP_REDIRECT }) (the helper defaults redirect_uri to the loopback REDIRECT, so the override is required); status 200, body.label 'iPhone', access_token matches /^odd_[0-9a-f]{64}$/, verifyDeviceToken resolves ok:true, SELECT platform FROM devices is 'ios-arm64'. Add test 'native sign-in with android-arm64 mints a device labelled Android phone' with the same steps and label 'Android phone'. Add an assertion that a fresh native code exchanged with redirect_uri 'http://127.0.0.1:4567/callback' returns { error: 'invalid_grant' }.

items.title: Given a PKCE sign-in with redirect_uri ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback and platform ios-arm64, when the GitHub callback completes, then the 302 Location is ai.overdeck.app:/oauth/callback with code=odc_... and the original state
When that code is exchanged at POST /oauth/token with the native redirect_uri and the matching verifier, then the response is 200 with label 'iPhone' and the devices row persists platform 'ios-arm64'
The same flow with platform android-arm64 returns label 'Android phone'
A native code exchanged with redirect_uri http://127.0.0.1:4567/callback returns 400 { error: 'invalid_grant' }
